title: xo timeline event (one line of timeline.jsonl)
description: Append-only event log. The file is JSONL — one JSON object per line, newline-terminated. This schema describes a single event. Validators should run line-by-line.

session_id.description: Set on most events; absent on project-wide events like `project.created`.

todo_status_changed.description: T7 made the HTTP API the todo event source and widened the timeline to carry EVERY status transition; sinks/timeline.py previously dropped all of them but completed. todo.completed keeps its own branch because it is the type readers, docs and the ?types= filter already know.

workitem_created.description: workitems-plan §8. Emitted by visualizer/workitems_store.py the moment a record exists in <project>/.xo/workitems.json — every workitem.* branch below is written by a store, never by a route, so the line exists exactly when the write it describes succeeded. `session_id` and `runtime` are absent when unknown: the workitem CRUD surface carries no session, and a placeholder id would name a session that never ran.

workitem_adopted.description: A workitem now mirrors a GitHub issue — either minted for it or an existing local record transitioned onto it. `issue` is nested because repo and number only mean anything together: a number without a repo names someone else's issue. Absent when the reference was unusable.

workitem_assigned.description: Who owes this workitem changed. `assignee` is REQUIRED and nullable: null is the un-assignment, and an absent key could not be told apart from an emitter that forgot. For an adopted item the write went to GitHub rather than to .xo/ (§5.3), so this line is the only local record of it.

workitem_claimed.description: An agent session started working this workitem. `in_progress` is DERIVED from a live claim and never stored (§5.4), so this line and its release are the only history the state ever had — which is what makes 'what did this agent work on last Tuesday' answerable without a stored flag that could have been wrong. `session_id` is required here precisely because a claim without one claims nothing.

workitem_released.description: A claim was dropped — explicitly, or implicitly by closing or tombstoning the workitem. NOT emitted when a claim simply lapses: a session going away is an absence of observation, not an event, and nothing writes at that moment (§5.4).

workitem_closed.description: A LOCAL workitem moved open -> closed. `state_reason` is GitHub's own vocabulary (completed / not_planned), never an invented one, and is omitted when unset. An adopted item is closed on GitHub, which this Space learns from the next poll and cannot emit here.

workitem_reopened.description: A local workitem moved closed -> open.

workitem_deleted.description: The workitem was tombstoned. The record itself is never removed (§5.1), so this marks the tombstone, not an erasure; `runtime` carries deleted_by when the caller attributed it.
